bundle.guidance:
# Academic Paper

Research notes, whitepapers and internal studies that should read like a
journal article: a narrow measure, a serif with real italics, numbered
sections, numbered figures and footnotes that are actually referenced.

## Principles

1. **The measure rules everything.** Roughly 65 characters per line
   (`--measure-column`). Long lines are the single fastest way to make a paper
   unreadable, and no amount of typography rescues them.
2. **Every claim is attributable.** A number, a figure or an assertion either
   carries a citation or is explicitly marked as this paper's own result.
3. **Structure is numeric.** Sections 1, 2, 2.1; figures Figure 1, 2; tables
   Table 1, 2. Cross-references use those numbers, never "above" or "below".

## Layout grid

One column of `--measure-column`, centred, giving a two-column journal feel
without the reflow problems of real columns. `--space-xl` between numbered
sections. Figures and tables may exceed the measure by up to 25% and are
always centred with the caption beneath (figures) or above (tables). An
abstract sits above section 1, indented on both sides.

## Typography

Crimson Pro (a Computer-Modern-adjacent serif) at `--size-body` with
`--line-body`. Headings are the same family in small caps or bold at
`--size-h1` / `--size-h2` / `--size-h3`; they are only slightly larger than
the body, as in a printed journal. Italics carry emphasis and defined terms;
bold is reserved for run-in heads. Mathematical and code fragments are
monospace.

## Colour usage

Near-black on warm off-white. The brick accent (`--color-brand-primary`) is
used only for internal links, footnote markers and the rule above a figure
caption. Charts use the palette in order but begin with black — a figure must
survive photocopying. Never colour a heading and never use a coloured
background for body text.

## Charts

Chart.js. Line and scatter for results, bar for categorical comparison. Axes
always labelled with units, error bars where the data has them, and a
`Figure N.` caption stating what the reader should conclude. Never a pie
chart. Keep to four series and distinguish them by dash pattern as well as
colour.

## Diagrams

Mermaid `flowchart TD` for method pipelines and `sequenceDiagram` for
protocols. Treat a diagram as a numbered figure with a caption, exactly like a
chart.

## Components and when to use each

- `abstract` — the 150–250 word summary above section 1. Exactly one.
- `numbered-section` — every heading; carries its own number.
- `figure` — a chart, diagram or image with a `Figure N.` caption below.
- `footnote` — an aside or a citation, marked in the text and collected at the
  end of the section.
- `reference-list` — the bibliography, numbered to match the in-text markers.

## Do / don't

- **Do** define every symbol and abbreviation at first use.
- **Do** state the limitations of the result in its own section.
- **Don't** use first person plural for work done by one person.
- **Don't** place a figure before it is first referenced in the text.
- **Don't** use bold for emphasis in running prose; use italics.

components.name: abstract
components.when_to_use: Exactly once, before the first numbered section.
components.html:
Abstract

We measure the cost of rebuilding an in-memory artifact index from object-storage tags and show that it is linear in the number of tags.

components.name: numbered-section
components.description: A numbered section heading with its body.
components.when_to_use: Every heading in the paper. Cross-reference by number only.
components.html:
2. Method

Each run hydrates a cold index from n tagged files and records wall-clock time.

components.name: figure
components.description: A chart, diagram or image with a numbered caption below.
components.when_to_use: Every visual. Place it after its first reference in the text.

components.name: footnote
components.description: An aside or citation, marked in text and collected per section.
components.when_to_use: For anything that would interrupt the argument; never for a required definition.
components.html:
The index is rebuilt on every start.1

  1. Storage Files are immutable, so no incremental rebuild exists.

components.name: reference-list
components.when_to_use: The last section of the paper; numbers match the in-text markers.
